text: The research file's territorial computation for the Kherson chapter uses DeepStateMap versions within a window of 31.5–34.3°E and 46.25–47.75°N, covering both banks of the Dnipro.

Latitude bounds of an analysis window

text: On the DeepStateMap version of 29 August 2022, the Russian-occupied area in the Kherson computation window (31.5–34.3°E, 46.25–47.75°N) was 17,672 km².
On the DeepStateMap version of 7 November 2022, the Russian-occupied area in the Kherson computation window (31.5–34.3°E, 46.25–47.75°N) was 16,230 km².

On the DeepStateMap version of 11 November 2022, 21:04 UTC, when "the entire right bank" was marked liberated, the Russian-occupied area in the Kherson computation window (31.5–34.3°E, 46.25–47.75°N) was 11,659 km².
By the research file's DeepStateMap computation, Ukraine regained about 1,440 km² in the Kherson ground offensive between 29 August and 7 November 2022.
By the research file's DeepStateMap computation, Ukraine regained about 4,570 km² in the Russian withdrawal of 7–11 November 2022.
By the research file's DeepStateMap computation, Ukraine regained roughly 6,000 km² in all in Kherson between 29 August and 11 November 2022.
After seizing Kherson in the first days of the full-scale invasion in 2022, Russia held a bridgehead on the right (west) bank of the Dnipro.

In 2022 the Russian bridgehead on the right bank of the Dnipro was supplied over three fixed crossings: the 1,366 m Antonivskyi road bridge, the Antonivskyi rail bridge 6 km upstream, and the road and rail crossing on the Kakhovka dam at Nova Kakhovka.

observations.subject: Antonivskyi rail bridge upstream of the road bridge

text: A single bridge at Darivka linked the two halves of the Russian right-bank bridgehead across the Inhulets in 2022.
From 19 July 2022 Ukraine struck the Dnipro crossings supplying the Russian Kherson bridgehead with US-supplied HIMARS.
The Antonivskyi road bridge closed to freight on 20 July 2022 after Ukrainian HIMARS strikes.
The Antonivskyi road bridge closed to all traffic after the night of 26–27 July 2022.
The Kakhovka dam crossing was declared unfit for use on 10 August 2022.
By mid-August 2022 the UK assessed that Russia had no bridge left that could carry heavy equipment across the Dnipro.
Russia adapted to the loss of the Dnipro bridges in 2022 with pontoon ferries, barges, a barge bridge and civilian river craft.
Russia reinforced its Kherson bridgehead in 2022 with much of its airborne force (VDV).
Ukraine's ground offensive in Kherson opened on 29 August 2022 from its Inhulets bridgehead and along the Mykolaiv line.
Ukraine's Kherson ground offensive of 2022 was heavily signalled, ran into prepared defences and was slow and costly.
Ukraine's Kherson offensive broke the northern sector along the Dnipro between 1 and 4 October 2022, at Zolota Balka, Dudchany and Davydiv Brid.
On 18 October 2022 the new Russian theatre commander, Army General Sergei Surovikin, spoke of "difficult decisions" in Kherson.
The Russian withdrawal across the Dnipro from Kherson appears to have begun on about 21–22 October 2022.
On 9 November 2022 Russian Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu and Army General Sergei Surovikin announced the withdrawal from Kherson on television.
Russia claimed it had completed its withdrawal from the Dnipro right bank at 05:00 on 11 November 2022.
Before completing its withdrawal on 11 November 2022, Russia blew up the Antonivskyi road and rail bridges, the road section on the Kakhovka dam and the Darivka bridge.
Ukrainian troops entered Kherson city on 11 November 2022 to cheering crowds on Freedom Square.
Russia withdrew its forces across the Dnipro from right-bank Kherson Oblast on 9–11 November 2022.
After the Russian withdrawal of 9–11 November 2022, Ukraine held all of right-bank Kherson Oblast and the previously occupied part of Mykolaiv Oblast.
Ukrainian forces entered Kherson city on 11 November 2022.
Ukraine did not cross the Dnipro in November 2022; its Kherson offensive culminated at the river.
Most of the Russian force on the Kherson right bank escaped across the Dnipro in the November 2022 withdrawal; the size of the force withdrawn is contested.
notes: OUTCOME; the bullet itself carries no citation; cites are those of its sub-points

text: The Russian MoD claimed that 30,000 personnel and 5,000 pieces of equipment were withdrawn from the Kherson right bank in November 2022 and that nothing was left behind.

observations.subject: Russian personnel withdrawn across the Dnipro

text: Other Russian sources said 20,000 men and 3,500 pieces of equipment were withdrawn from the Kherson right bank over three days in November 2022.

observations.subject: Russian men withdrawn across the Dnipro

text: Russian withdrawal schedules published by Ukrainian journalist Andriy Tsaplienko list 42,370 troops, 253 tanks, almost 400 APCs and several thousand wheeled vehicles on the Kherson right bank in 2022.

observations.subject: Russian troops in the withdrawal schedules

text: The Russian withdrawal schedules published by Andriy Tsaplienko show more than 6,000 pieces of equipment ferried across the Dnipro between 21 October and 7 November 2022.

observations.subject: pieces of Russian equipment ferried across

observations.subject: Russian troops on the Kherson right bank

text: Russian losses in the November 2022 Dnipro crossing itself were small and are not counted.
After the Russian withdrawal from Kherson in November 2022 there were abandoned helicopters and armoured vehicles, prisoners, and Russian soldiers in civilian clothes left on the right bank.
The central spans of the Antonivskyi road bridge, the Antonivskyi rail bridge, the Kakhovka dam road and the Darivka bridge were destroyed on 11 November 2022.
Satellite imagery showed at least seven bridges destroyed in the Kherson area in 24 hours around 11 November 2022, four of them across the Dnipro.
Valerii Zaluzhnyi said on 10 November 2022 that 41 settlements had been retaken in the Kherson direction since 1 October.
Volodymyr Zelensky said that more than 60 settlements had been retaken in Kherson by 12 November 2022.
Wikipedia puts the area Russia ceded in the November 2022 Kherson withdrawal at about 40% of Kherson Oblast.

observations.subject: share of Kherson Oblast ceded by Russia

text: Ukraine reached the Dnipro along its whole right bank in Kherson by about 11–12 November 2022.
ISW assessed that Russia withdrew from the Kherson right bank in November 2022 "in relatively good order".
Some sources, including Miller, argue that a more aggressive Ukrainian pursuit in November 2022 could have caught more of the Russian Kherson force.
Ukraine's commander rated the 2022 Kherson operation only "50–60% successful".

text: On 9 July 2022 Volodymyr Zelensky ordered the military, including Operational Command South, to retake the occupied south of Ukraine.
On 9 July 2022 Iryna Vereshchuk urged residents of occupied Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts to evacuate.
On 10 July 2022 a Ukrainian strike hit a Russian base in Kherson city.

mentions.name: Strike on Russian base in Kherson (10 July 2022)

text: Russian and Ukrainian sources reported that the commander of the 20th Guards Motor Rifle Division, Col. Gorobets, and two of his deputies were killed in the Ukrainian strike on a Kherson base on 10 July 2022.
Ukraine claimed that the chief of staff of the Russian 22nd Army Corps was also killed in the strike on a Kherson base on 10 July 2022.
On 11 July 2022 Ukraine carried out a HIMARS strike on Nova Kakhovka.
On 11 July 2022 Ukraine's 60th Mechanised Brigade took Ivanivka.
The first reported HIMARS strike on the Antonivskyi road bridge came on 19 July 2022 and did little visible damage.
One analyst (Miller) dates the first HIMARS strike on the Antonivskyi road bridge to 20 July 2022 rather than 19 July.
On 20 July 2022 a second Ukrainian strike hit the Antonivskyi road bridge, and Vladimir Saldo closed it to freight while leaving it open to cars.
In the 20 July 2022 strike on the Antonivskyi road bridge, eight rockets reportedly landed within a 20 m circle.

metric_new.label: Size of the area a salvo landed within

observations.note: 'within a 20 m circle'; diameter vs radius not stated

text: On about 22 July 2022 seven HIMARS rockets reportedly hit the Darivka bridge and the Kakhovka dam bridge.
At about 22:55 on 26 July 2022 a third Ukrainian strike put eight rockets on the Antonivskyi road bridge and two on the Antonivskyi rail bridge.
After the strike of 26 July 2022 the Antonivskyi road bridge was closed to all traffic and the Antonivskyi rail bridge was damaged.
The Russian MoD claimed ten rockets intercepted in the Ukrainian strike on the Antonivskyi bridges on 26–27 July 2022.
On 27 July 2022 Ukraine said it had retaken Lozove and Andriivka on the east bank of the Inhulets, its bridgehead.
On 29 July 2022 four Russian pontoon bridging columns were seen beside the Antonivskyi road bridge and another near the rail bridge.

observations.subject: pontoon bridging columns beside the road bridge

text: On 29 July 2022 Ukraine struck the Russian pontoon bridging columns gathered by the Antonivskyi bridges.
On 30 July 2022 a HIMARS strike hit a 40-car train at Brylivka.

observations.subject: rail cars in the train struck

text: Ukraine claimed 80 Russians killed and 200 wounded in the HIMARS strike on a train at Brylivka on 30 July 2022.
On 31 July 2022 Russian forces dug trenches at the bridgehead end of the Antonivskyi bridges.
By 31 July 2022 Russia had set radar reflectors along both Antonivskyi bridges.
On 31 July 2022 Russia was trying to repair the Antonivskyi road bridge.
On 1 August 2022 four more HIMARS launchers and German MARS II launchers arrived in Ukraine.
On 10 August 2022 Operational Command South declared the Kakhovka dam bridge unfit for use.
On 13 August 2022 the Kakhovka dam bridge was hit again.
On 13 August 2022 the UK MoD said no bridge across the Dnipro could carry heavy equipment and that Russia was relying on a pontoon ferry by the Antonivskyi road bridge.
On 17 August 2022 barges were seen on the Dnipro by Kherson city.
On 17 August 2022 Russians were reported repairing barges at a Kherson city shipyard.
Between 20 and 23 August 2022 a limited Russian push east of Mykolaiv took Blahodatne.
On 21 August 2022 geolocated imagery showed repaired barges ferrying material across the Dnipro near Kherson city.
On 22–23 August 2022 Ukraine struck the site of the Russian 247th Guards Air Assault Regiment.
On 22–23 August 2022 Ukraine struck the Chornobaivka ammunition depot.
Wikipedia reports that repairs to the Antonivskyi road bridge were completed on 23 August 2022; satellite imagery two days later contests this.
On 24–25 August 2022 Ukraine struck the Antonivskyi bridge again to stop repair crews, and struck the Kakhovka bridge area.
Satellite imagery in late August 2022 showed at least 16 holes at the southern end of the Antonivskyi road bridge.

observations.subject: holes in the Antonivskyi road bridge deck

text: Satellite imagery in late August 2022 showed ferry queues and a Russian pontoon bridge about 60% built by the Antonivskyi road bridge.
By 25 August 2022 imagery showed about 100 vehicles moving north across the Dnipro by ferry.
On 29 August 2022 Ukraine announced its Kherson counteroffensive and broke through the Russian "first line".
On 29 August 2022 the DNR 109th Regiment abandoned its positions.
On 29 August 2022 Ukrainian forces entered Arkhanhelske.
On 29 August 2022 Ukraine struck the Lvove pontoon ferry and a barge crossing by the Antonivskyi road bridge.
On 30 August 2022 Ukraine struck the Antonivskyi road and rail bridges and the Darivka bridge.
On 30 August 2022 the Russian MoD claimed 44 HIMARS rockets intercepted.
On 1 September 2022 the Darivka pontoon bridge over the Inhulets was destroyed.
On 1 September 2022 the command posts of the Russian 331st Regiment (98th VDV Division) and 56th Regiment (7th VDV Division) were reported hit.
On 2 September 2022 Zakarpattia held a day of mourning for the dead of the 128th Mountain Assault Brigade.
On 2 September 2022 HIMARS hit the Antonivskyi road bridge, ferry boats and barges.
On 2 September 2022 Ukraine struck the Russian ferries at Lvove and Kozatske.
On 4 September 2022 a Ukrainian flag was raised in Vysokopillia.
Imagery of 4 September 2022 showed the Nova Kakhovka road bridge collapsed and the rail bridge "tipped on its edge".
On 6 September 2022 Ukraine's Kharkiv offensive began and broke through quickly.
By 7 September 2022 one Russian ferry by the Antonivskyi road bridge was out of service.
On 7 September 2022 Russia opened a new ferry crossing in downtown Kherson.
On 7 September 2022 Ukraine struck a Russian convoy on a pontoon near Nova Kakhovka.
On 8 September 2022 Mark Milley said the US had sent Ukraine 16 HIMARS and "thousands" of GMLRS rockets, and that Ukraine had hit more than 400 targets with them.

observations.subject: HIMARS launchers sent by the US

text: On 8 September 2022 the UK MoD confirmed that the Darivka ferry had been eliminated.
Between 9 and 12 September 2022 Ukraine claimed that the Russian 247th Air Assault Regiment (about 1,500 men) "no longer exists".
Between 9 and 12 September 2022 Ukraine claimed that the Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade had lost 85% or more of its strength.
On the evening of 14 September 2022 Russian missiles breached the Karachunivske reservoir dam at Kryvyi Rih.
After Russian missiles breached the Karachunivske dam on 14 September 2022, the Inhulets rose by 1–2 m downstream.

metric_new.label: Change in river or reservoir water level

text: Around 23–24 September 2022 there were reports that Vladimir Putin refused his commanders' request to fall back from Kherson.
Around 23–24 September 2022 Russia rotated units in Kherson and built defence lines further back.
On 1 October 2022 Ukraine broke through at Zolota Balka and took Khreshchenivka.
On 1 October 2022 Russian forces fell back to Mykhailivka.
On 2 October 2022 Russian forces likely fell back 24 km to Dudchany.
On 2 October 2022 Ukraine's 35th Marine Brigade crossed the Inhulets.
On 3 October 2022 Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the liberation of Arkhanhelske and Myroliubivka.
On 3 October 2022 Ukrainian forces advanced along the T0403 road.
On 4 October 2022 Davydiv Brid fell to Ukraine's 35th Marine Brigade and half of Dudchany was taken.
On 4 October 2022 Russian forces abandoned about 20 villages to avoid encirclement, and ISW described the northeastern Russian line along the Kakhovka reservoir as "collapsing".
On 8 October 2022 a truck bomb damaged the Kerch Strait (Crimean) bridge.
ISW judged that the damage to the Crimean Bridge on 8 October 2022 further strained Russian supply to the south and contributed to the Kherson withdrawal decision.
On 9 October 2022 Ukraine said it had retaken 1,170 km² in the south.
On 13 October 2022 Vladimir Saldo asked for a mass evacuation from Kherson.
Around 13 October 2022 Ukraine targeted Russian pontoon and barge crossings on the Dnipro and Inhulets.
Around 13 October 2022 Russia was reported repairing up to 30 armoured vehicles a day at Kalanchak.
On 18 October 2022 Sergei Surovikin said on television that the situation in Kherson was "not easy" and that Russia faced "difficult decisions".
On 18 October 2022 Sergei Surovikin claimed that Ukraine planned to breach the Kakhovka dam.
On 18 October 2022 Vladimir Saldo announced a "gradual displacement" of residents from four towns.
On 20 October 2022 Ukraine struck a Russian repair base in Nova Kakhovka.
Around 20 October 2022 RFE/RL geolocated a Russian ferry carrying equipment at Kozatske.
The captured Russian schedule shows a phased withdrawal from the Kherson right bank beginning on 21 October 2022 and running to 7 November.
On 22 October 2022 Kherson residents were ordered to "leave immediately".
On 22 October 2022 the UK MoD said a Russian barge bridge had been completed beside the Antonivskyi road bridge.
By 22 October 2022 Russian officers were being moved across the Dnipro while mobilised men stayed on the Kherson right bank as the force left in contact.
In October 2022, without announcing it, Kyiv replaced Maj. Gen. Andrii Kovalchuk with Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi as commander of the Kherson operation because it judged the operation too slow.
In late October 2022 Ramzan Kadyrov admitted that 23 of his fighters had been killed and 58 wounded by artillery in Kherson.
In late October 2022 Kyrylo Budanov said at least 40,000 Russian troops were in Kherson.
On 8 November 2022 there was no internet in Kherson city.
On 8 November 2022 pillboxes were seen at Hola Prystan on the left bank of the Dnipro.
The US midterm elections took place on 8 November 2022, the day before Russia announced its Kherson withdrawal.
On 9 November 2022 a televised meeting between Sergei Shoigu and Sergei Surovikin ordered the Russian withdrawal from Kherson to the left bank of the Dnipro.
On 9 November 2022 occupation deputy head Kirill Stremousov died in a "car crash".
On 9 November 2022 bridges near Snihurivka were blown.
On 10 November 2022 Ukraine advanced up to 7 km and took 12 settlements, over 260 km² in a day.
On 10 November 2022 Ukraine's 131st Reconnaissance Battalion took Snihurivka.
On 10 November 2022 Ukraine's 28th Mechanised Brigade took Kyselivka.
By the evening of 10 November 2022 Ukrainian officials estimated that half the Russian force had crossed the Dnipro.

observations.subject: share of the Russian force across the Dnipro

text: On the night of 10–11 November 2022 a Ukrainian flag was raised in central Kherson, apparently by partisans.
On the night of 10–11 November 2022 Russian infantry were filmed crossing a pontoon bridge by the Antonivskyi bridge.
At 05:00 on 11 November 2022 the Russian MoD declared its withdrawal from the Kherson right bank complete.
notes: ISW gives 05:00 local time; Wikipedia gives 05:00 Moscow time

text: On 11 November 2022 the Antonivskyi road and rail bridges, the Kakhovka dam road and the Darivka bridge were destroyed, as shown by Maxar imagery.
On 11 November 2022 Ukrainian troops entered Kherson along the T1501 and M14 roads, with special forces in the lead.
On 11 November 2022 Ukrainian forces entered Beryslav and Tiahynka.
At 21:04 UTC on 11 November 2022 DeepStateMap marked the whole right bank of Kherson and Mykolaiv oblasts as liberated.
By 12 November 2022 over 60 settlements had been retaken in Kherson and Ukrainian units had reached the Dnipro.
On 12 November 2022 Henichesk became the "temporary" capital of the Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast.
On 12 November 2022 abandoned Russian helicopters and armoured vehicles were found on the Kherson right bank.
On 14 November 2022 Volodymyr Zelensky visited liberated Kherson.
On 14 November 2022 Valerii Zaluzhnyi thanked the units involved and said the Kherson operation "has its price".
The Kherson chapter map runs from the Inhulets bridgehead and the Kherson–Dnipropetrovsk oblast border (Arkhanhelske, Vysokopillia) in the north to the Dnipro and its estuary in the south.
The Kherson chapter map runs from the Mykolaiv line (Posad-Pokrovske, Snihurivka) in the west to the Kakhovka dam in the east.
In the Kherson chapter map the left-bank Russian rear (Oleshky, Hola Prystan, Nova Kakhovka, Kalanchak) is the depot zone.
Coordinates in the Kherson chapter come from OSM Nominatim unless a bridge's own Wikipedia infobox is cited, and its distances are the research file's great-circle computations from those points.
The Antonivskyi road bridge is at 46.6700, 32.7203 (lat, lon).
The Antonivskyi road bridge is a 1,366 m box-girder bridge on 31 piers, opened in 1985.

observations.subject: piers of the Antonivskyi road bridge

text: The Antonivskyi road bridge carries the M14 (formerly M17) from Antonivka to Dachi and Oleshky.
The Antonivskyi road bridge was the main road supply route for the Russian Kherson bridgehead in 2022.
Ukraine struck the Antonivskyi road bridge from 19 or 20 July 2022, and its spans were dropped on 11 November 2022.
The Antonivskyi rail bridge is at 46.6754, 32.7970 (lat, lon).
The Antonivskyi rail bridge is a single-track bridge "nearly one kilometre" long, opened in 1954, at river km 43.5 near the mouth of the Inhulets, about 6 km upstream of the Antonivskyi road bridge.

observations.subject: rail bridge upstream of road bridge

text: Ukraine struck the Antonivskyi rail bridge from 27 July 2022, and it was destroyed on 11 November 2022.
Russia ran a fuel pipeline along the Antonivskyi rail bridge in 2022.
The Kakhovka dam road and rail crossing (R47) is at 46.7761, 33.3717 (lat, lon).
The Kakhovka dam is 3,273 m long and 30 m high; one source gives its bridge section as about 500 m in 22 spans.

observations.subject: spans of the Kakhovka dam bridge section

text: The Kakhovka dam crossing was unfit from 10 August 2022, its road had collapsed by 4 September, and its road section was blown on 11 November 2022.
The Kakhovka dam itself held after the November 2022 demolition of its road section until 6 June 2023.
The village of Darivka is at 46.7483, 32.7930 (lat, lon); the Darivka bridge itself was not geolocated.
notes: geo: 32.7930,46.7483; village centre, not the bridge

text: The Darivka bridge over the Inhulets is on the Kherson–Nova Kakhovka road (E58), about 18 km from Kherson.

In 2022 the Darivka bridge was the only link between the two halves of the Russian Kherson bridgehead; the pontoon alongside it was destroyed about 1 September and the bridge was blown on 11 November.
The Russian ferry and pontoon site at Lvove is at 46.7911, 33.1492 (lat, lon).
The Russian ferry and pontoon site at Kozatske is at 46.7855, 33.3503 (lat, lon).
The Russian ferry and pontoon site at Beryslav is at 46.8358, 33.4167 (lat, lon).
Russian ferry and pontoon sites in 2022 also lay by both Antonivskyi bridges and in downtown Kherson from 7 September.
By early September 2022 Russia had two ferries at Kherson, three around Nova Kakhovka and one at Darivka.
By 22 October 2022 Russia had a barge bridge by the Antonivskyi road bridge.
Kherson is at 46.6401, 32.6144 (lat, lon).
By the research file's great-circle computation, Kherson city is about 8.7 km from the Antonivskyi road bridge, 58 km from Nova Kakhovka and 18 km from Darivka.
Nova Kakhovka is at 46.7583, 33.3567 (lat, lon).
By the research file's great-circle computation, the two Antonivskyi bridges are 5.9 km apart, and the Antonivskyi road bridge is 51 km from the Kakhovka dam.

observations.subject: Antonivskyi road bridge to Kakhovka dam

text: Davydiv Brid is at 47.2409, 33.1935 (lat, lon) and lies on the Inhulets.
By the research file's great-circle computation, Davydiv Brid is 73 km from the Antonivskyi road bridge.

observations.subject: Davydiv Brid to Antonivskyi road bridge

text: Dudchany is at 47.1914, 33.7803 (lat, lon) and lies on the Kakhovka reservoir shore.
Arkhanhelske is at 47.4318, 33.4054 (lat, lon).
By the research file's great-circle computation, Dudchany is 48 km north of Beryslav and Arkhanhelske is 66 km from Beryslav.
Snihurivka is at 47.0707, 32.7925 (lat, lon).
By the research file's great-circle computation, Snihurivka is 50 km from Kherson.
Posad-Pokrovske is at 46.8021, 32.2681 (lat, lon), on the Ukrainian line in 2022.

The Ukrainian line at Posad-Pokrovske was 37.5 km from the Antonivskyi road bridge and 84 km from the Kakhovka dam, against a GMLRS range of about 80 km, so the dam was at the edge of reach from the Mykolaiv side and closer from the north.
Oleshky is at 46.6261, 32.7220 (lat, lon), just across the Antonivskyi road bridge in the Russian rear.
Hola Prystan is at 46.5320, 32.5345 (lat, lon), in the Russian rear.
Radensk is at 46.5511, 32.9256 (lat, lon), a Russian depot in the rear.
Brylivka is at 46.4202, 33.1411 (lat, lon), the Russian railhead.
Kalanchak is at 46.2572, 33.2844 (lat, lon), site of Russian repair yards.
The ground of right-bank Kherson is flat steppe farmland cut by shelterbelts.
Kherson Oblast has about 30,000 km of windbreaks.
In Oleshky district the shelterbelts are 350–780 m apart.
The Inhulets runs north–south and was the de facto front line in Kherson from March 2022.
Ukraine's foothold on the east bank of the Inhulets (Lozove, Andriivka, Bilohirka, Sukhyi Stavok) was the springboard of its 29 August 2022 offensive.
The northern sector of the Kherson front runs along the Kakhovka reservoir on the T0403 road.
One Russian milblogger complained in October 2022 that the northern Kherson sector was held at one man per 60 m of front, with some villages defended by 15 men.
Russia built three defence lines around Kherson city in 2022.
Wounded Ukrainians described Russian tanks firing from concrete shelters in Kherson in 2022.
Russia lowered the Kakhovka reservoir from late October 2022.
Weather and light data in the Kherson chapter are ERA5 reanalysis values for Kherson city.
In Kherson city on 19–20 July 2022 the weather was dry, at 27–29 °C with 33–36% cloud, and daylight ran from 05:14 to 20:36.
In Kherson city on 26–27 July 2022, the night of the third bridge strike, the weather was clear, with 15–16% cloud and up to 32 °C.
In Kherson city on 29–30 August 2022 the weather was hot and clear, at 32–33 °C with 7–15% cloud, and sunset was about 19:34.
On 2 October 2022 Kherson city had rain of 14.9 mm with wind up to 25 km/h.
On 4 October 2022 Kherson city was dry, at 9–17 °C.
In Kherson city on 9–11 November 2022 the weather was dry, at 1–11 °C with light wind (about 8 km/h maximum), and daylight ran from about 07:45 to 17:20.
Kherson city was overcast on 11 November 2022 (96% cloud), which hid the final Russian Dnipro crossings from optical satellites by day.
Daily minimum temperatures in Kherson city stayed above 0 °C from 15 July to 15 November 2022, so the Dnipro did not freeze during the Russian withdrawal.

The 49th Combined Arms Army (Southern Military District) was the main Russian force on the Kherson right bank in 2022, with two motor-rifle brigades, the 205th and 34th, plus a tank battalion, about 10,000 men as of July.

observations.subject: 49th Combined Arms Army on the Kherson right bank

text: The Russian 22nd Army Corps (Crimea) held the southern half of the Kherson right-bank bridgehead in 2022.
In summer 2022 Russia reinforced the Kherson right bank with the 7th Guards Air Assault Division's 247th Regiment at Kherson airport, its 108th Regiment at Blahodatne and its 56th Regiment.

text: The commanders of the Russian Kherson grouping are not named in the sources gathered; Army General Sergei Surovikin was theatre commander from October 2022.
Ukraine claimed that the Russian 247th Air Assault Regiment (about 1,500 men) "no longer existed" by 9 September 2022.
Ukraine claimed that the Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade (about 2,500 men) had lost 85% or more by 12 September 2022.
Ukraine claimed that the Russian 126th Coastal Defence Brigade (about 2,000 men) was "degraded, if not destroyed" by 4 October 2022; its men complained of one BTR per 80 soldiers.

observations.subject: soldiers per BTR in the 126th Brigade

text: Ukraine claimed 2,500 Russians killed and 5,000 wounded on the Kherson front from 29 August to 29 September 2022.
The Russian MoD admitted 1,200–1,360 killed and wounded on the Kherson front in the 2022 offensive.
notes: period not stated precisely in the text; listed with the 29 Aug–29 Sep claims

text: Ukraine claimed heavy losses among the Russian 247th Air Assault Regiment, 810th Naval Infantry Brigade and 126th Coastal Defence Brigade on the Kherson front in September–October 2022.
notes: summary of the source line for the c04/0021 attrition list

text: From October 2022 mobilised men reinforced the Russian 205th Motor Rifle Brigade and 810th Naval Infantry Brigade on the Kherson right bank.
In the 2022 Kherson withdrawal Russian officers were moved across the Dnipro first, leaving newly mobilised men as the rearguard.
Maj. Gen. Andrii Kovalchuk at first commanded Ukraine's Operational Command South in the 2022 Kherson offensive, and Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi took over in October.
Ukraine's "Kakhovka" operational group fought in the northern sector of the Kherson front in 2022.
Ukraine's Operational Command South fielded about three dozen army, marine and territorial battalions in the Kherson offensive, perhaps 20,000 combat troops.
Ukraine's 28th Mechanised Brigade fought in the Oleksandrivka and Posad-Pokrovske sector, then took Kyselivka on 10 November 2022 and entered Kherson on 11–12 November.
Volodymyr Zelensky named the 59th Motorised and 63rd Mechanised Brigades, with the 28th, as the liberators of Kherson in November 2022.
Ukraine's 57th Motorised Brigade fought at Velyke Artakove, Bila Krynytsia, Andriivka and Sukhyi Stavok in the 2022 Kherson offensive.
Ukraine's 60th Mechanised Brigade took Ivanivka in July 2022, then sent one battalion, with one of the 128th Brigade's, in the October drive on Zolota Balka, Dudchany and Mylove.
Ukraine's 60th Mechanised Brigade had had no break from combat since February 2022 by the Kherson offensive.
Ukraine's 128th Mountain Assault Brigade took heavy losses in the first days of the Kherson offensive in 2022, then took Myroliubivka on 3 October.
Ukraine's 35th and 36th Marine Brigades led the push south from the Inhulets, fighting at Bruskynske and taking Davydiv Brid on 4 October 2022.
Russian sources reported Ukraine's 46th Airmobile Brigade near Ishchenka in October 2022.
Ukraine's 131st Reconnaissance Battalion took Snihurivka in the 2022 Kherson offensive.
Ukrainian Special Operations Forces, the GUR, the National Guard and partisans also took part in the 2022 Kherson operation.
Ukraine had 4 HIMARS by 24 June 2022 and 8 by mid-July.
Four more HIMARS arrived in Ukraine on 1 August 2022 together with German MARS II launchers.
By 8 September 2022 the US had sent Ukraine 16 HIMARS launchers and "thousands" of GMLRS rockets.

observations.subject: HIMARS launchers sent by the US

text: British M270 launchers were in Ukrainian service from July 2022.
No source splits Ukraine's HIMARS and other launchers between the Kherson and Kharkiv fronts in 2022.
Ukraine published no figures for its own losses in the 2022 Kherson offensive.
notes: uncited in text; cites the sub-points' source as background

text: Wounded Ukrainian soldiers interviewed by the Washington Post in 2022 spoke of Kherson units with almost all 120 men wounded, 7 killed and 20 wounded out of 100, and 16 of 32 wounded.

observations.subject: men wounded in one unit of 120

text: One wounded Ukrainian soldier said of the 2022 Kherson offensive: "We lost five people for every one they did".

cites.quote: We lost five people for every one they did

observations.note: Ukrainian losses per Russian loss, one soldier's account

text: RUSI counts the 2022 Kherson push, with the Donbas defence, among the two main sources of the roughly 30,000 Ukrainian killed and missing in 2022.

observations.subject: Ukrainian killed and missing in 2022 (all fronts)

text: Russia claimed 9,500 Ukrainian killed and wounded in the 2022 Kherson offensive.
Russian missiles on the Karachunivske dam raised the Inhulets by 1–2 m on 14–15 September 2022.

metric_new.label: Change in river or reservoir water level

text: GMLRS rockets reach about 80 km.
GMLRS has a CEP of "less than a meter".
Ukraine fired small HIMARS salvoes at the same aim point on the Kherson bridges in July 2022: 8 rockets on 20 July, 7 at Darivka and the Kakhovka dam on about 22 July, and 8 + 2 on 26–27 July.

observations.subject: GMLRS rockets on the Antonivskyi road bridge
GMLRS rockets at Darivka and the Kakhovka dam
GMLRS rockets on the road (8) and rail (2) bridges

text: Ukraine's small HIMARS salvoes on the Kherson bridges in 2022 cratered the deck rather than dropping spans, and the strikes were repeated whenever repairs began.
TWZ reports that Ukraine deliberately hit only one small segment of the Antonivskyi road bridge so that it could be repaired after liberation.
Russian claims of HIMARS interceptions over the Kherson bridges (10 on 27 July and 44 on 30 July 2022) are not borne out by footage.
notes: text gives 30 Jul for the 44 claim; the timeline gives 30 Aug (isw-2022-08-30-roca); likely a typo for 30 Aug

text: In 2022 Ukrainian HIMARS strikes hit the Kherson base on 10 July, the Nova Kakhovka depots, Radensk, the Brylivka train on 30 July, Chornobaivka, VDV regimental command posts on 1 September, and repair bases.
8–12 HIMARS launchers wrecked most Russian depots in the south and Donbas within weeks in 2022, and Russian depots moved beyond about 85 km from the front.
The US counted more than 400 targets hit by Ukrainian HIMARS by 8 September 2022.
After the 2022 HIMARS strikes Russia could no longer stockpile ammunition beside its guns.
Ukraine reportedly also used Excalibur and possibly Vulcano 155 mm rounds against Russian crossings and depots in Kherson in 2022.
Ukraine used HARM missiles against Russian air defence in the Kherson campaign in 2022.
Russia claimed HARM missiles were shot down over the Antonivskyi bridge on 1 September 2022.
Russia set radar reflectors on the Antonivskyi bridges in 2022 to counter Ukrainian interdiction.
Russia rapidly repaired the Antonivskyi road bridge deck in 2022, and Ukraine struck it again each time.
Russia ran pontoon ferries manoeuvred by river boats at up to six sites across the Dnipro in 2022.
Russia used repaired barges, then a barge bridge, then civilian ferries and barges commandeered from Kherson port to cross the Dnipro in 2022; the civilian craft were hard to target.
Russia ran a fuel pipeline along the Antonivskyi rail bridge in 2022.
Russia moved its Kherson logistics deeper in 2022, to repair yards at Kalanchak and a new base about 70 km southeast of Kherson.

observations.subject: new Russian base southeast of Kherson

text: Russian ferries on the Dnipro were inefficient: about 100 vehicles were seen moving north by ferry by 25 August 2022.
Because hitting a ferry has a shorter-lived effect than closing a bridge, ISW dates the systematic Ukrainian ferry strikes to the opening of the Kherson ground offensive on 29 August 2022.
Ukraine hit Russian bridging columns by the Antonivskyi bridges as early as 29 July 2022.
In the 2022 defence of the Kherson bridgehead Russia relied on Orlan-10 UAVs spotting from more than 1 km up.
In the 2022 defence of the Kherson bridgehead Russia used counter-battery radar and tanks in concrete shelters.
In one Ukrainian soldier's account, Russian mortars in Kherson in 2022 answered three Ukrainian rounds with 20.
In the 2022 Kherson fighting Russian EW hijacked Ukrainian drones and Russia used direction-finding of phones.
ATGM ambushes and artillery killing areas inside three prepared lines completed the Russian defence of the Kherson bridgehead in 2022.
Russia struck the Karachunivske dam in September 2022 to flood the Inhulets.
From October 2022 Russia drew down the Kakhovka reservoir while warning of a Ukrainian "false flag" attack on the Kakhovka dam.
Ukraine considered using HIMARS on the Kakhovka dam to raise the river as a "last resort" in 2022 and did not do so.
Russia blew bridges near Snihurivka on 9 November 2022.
On 11 November 2022 Russia blew the four main Dnipro and Inhulets bridges, the Kherson TV tower, the heat and power plant and other utilities.
Russia left mines and booby traps in Kherson city when it withdrew in November 2022.

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
rationale: Russia set radar reflectors along both Antonivskyi bridges as a counter to HIMARS interdiction (text lists them among Russian counters; no effect stated).

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
effect: restores limited traffic until the next strike
rationale: Russia repaired the cratered deck quickly, but each repair was struck again.

counter: repeated GMLRS re-strikes on repair work
rationale: Ukraine repeated the strikes whenever repairs began, so repairs never restored the crossing.

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
rationale: With the bridges closed Russia shifted to pontoon ferries at up to six sites, but they were inefficient (about 100 vehicles north by 25 Aug).

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
rationale: Russia used repaired barges and then a barge bridge to replace the struck bridges.

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
rationale: Civilian craft taken from Kherson port were hard to target.

counter: fuel pipeline along the rail bridge
measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
rationale: A fuel pipeline along the Antonivskyi rail bridge kept fuel flowing despite the strikes.

measure: HIMARS/GMLRS precision strikes on bridges and depots
effect: depots out of reach; no ammunition stockpiles beside the guns
rationale: Russian depots moved beyond about 85 km and logistics moved deeper to Kalanchak and a base about 70 km southeast of Kherson.
Ukraine struck the ferries systematically from 29 August, though a hit ferry is replaced sooner than a closed bridge.
Russian EW hijacked Ukrainian drones in the Kherson fighting.

measure: Russian air defence covering the crossings
rationale: Ukraine used HARM against air defence during the interdiction campaign.

text: At about 22:55 on 26 July 2022 eight rockets hit the Antonivskyi road bridge and two hit the Antonivskyi rail bridge 6 km upstream.
In the strike of 26–27 July 2022 on the Antonivskyi bridges, Russian air defence lit up only after the impacts.
On the morning of 27 July 2022 the Antonivskyi road bridge deck was holed across its full width, and the occupation administration closed the bridge to all traffic.
A Ukrainian newspaper called the Antonivskyi road bridge "cheese" after the strike of 26–27 July 2022.
The weather on the night of 26–27 July 2022 at Kherson was clear and warm.
In 2022 Russian pontoon ferries shuttled across the Dnipro under the Kakhovka dam and at Lvove, 16 km downstream.

observations.subject: Lvove downstream of the Kakhovka dam

text: Each Russian pontoon ferry on the Dnipro was a moving target that Ukraine had to find and time.
Ukraine struck the Russian ferries at Lvove and Kozatske from 29 August 2022, and Russia rebuilt them.
In October 2022 a Luhansk soldier filmed himself on a loaded Russian ferry heading for the Nova Kakhovka canal mouth, and RFE/RL geolocated the video.
An intercepted Russian officer complained of "12 cars… transported by pontoon" lost to the bottom of the Dnipro.
notes: date not given; placed in the ferry war (Aug–Oct 2022)

text: On 29 August 2022, after weeks of strikes, Ukraine attacked out of the Inhulets bridgehead on several axes.
On 29 August 2022 the forcibly mobilised DNR 109th Regiment fled Arkhanhelske.
On 29 August 2022 Ukrainian units pushed about 6 km from the Inhulets bridgehead toward Sukhyi Stavok.
Within days of the 29 August 2022 attack Zakarpattia mourned the dead of the 128th Mountain Assault Brigade.
In early September 2022 hospitals in southern Ukraine filled with men wounded by cluster munitions and mortars in the Kherson offensive.
On 1–4 October 2022 a battalion each of the 128th and 60th Brigades broke through at Zolota Balka and rolled south along the Kakhovka reservoir road.
In early October 2022 the 35th Marine Brigade crossed the Inhulets and took Davydiv Brid.
About 20 villages were abandoned by Russian forces in a day in the Dudchany collapse of early October 2022.

observations.subject: villages abandoned by Russian forces in a day

text: At a staged meeting on 9 November 2022 Sergei Surovikin recommended defending "along the barrier line of the Dnipro River", and Sergei Shoigu agreed.

cites.quote: along the barrier line of the Dnipro River

text: On 9 November 2022 the occupation deputy head Kirill Stremousov died in a car crash.
On the night of 10–11 November 2022 Russian infantry walked over the pontoon bridge beside the Antonivskyi bridge in the dark.
After the last Russian crossing on 11 November 2022 the central spans of the Antonivskyi road bridge went into the river, along with the rail bridge, the Kakhovka dam road and the Darivka bridge.
Some Russian stragglers on the Kherson right bank were told in November 2022 to "change into civilian clothing" and get out any way they could.
Some Russian soldiers drowned trying to swim the Dnipro during the November 2022 withdrawal.
On 11 November 2022 Ukrainian troops drove into Kherson along the M14 and T1501.
On 11 November 2022 crowds in Kherson's Freedom Square chanted "Glory to the ZSU" and lifted a female Ukrainian soldier onto their shoulders.
On the night of 11 November 2022 Kherson residents danced around a bonfire singing "Chervona Kalyna".

In summer 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff, with US and UK planners, judged a thrust from Zaporizhzhia to Melitopol, which would also cut the Kherson grouping's supply, the most attractive option but too risky against the main Russian concentration, and chose Kherson, where the river would protect its gains.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Allied wargames in summer 2022 reportedly showed that Ukraine lacked the means for a Zaporizhzhia–Melitopol offensive.
Ukraine announced its Kherson push for months in June–August 2022 because it needed a visible "win" for its partners, and RUSI judges that this cost Ukraine surprise.
Commentators such as Phillips O'Brien and ISW argue that Ukraine's signalling of the Kherson offensive drew Russian reserves south, onto the far side of bridges under fire, and opened Kharkiv.
In summer 2022 the Russian command sent its VDV "fire brigade" and about a dozen battalions from Donbas to the Kherson bridgehead, across a river it could not supply reliably.
Russia's reinforcement of Kherson in 2022 hollowed out the Kharkiv front, where the Russian line collapsed.
The Ukrainian plan in 2022 was reportedly for the Kharkiv offensive on about 4 September and the Kherson offensive on about 18 September, after two weeks of shelling.
Volodymyr Zelensky moved the Kherson offensive forward to 29 August 2022 for political effect before the UN General Assembly, and a US general warned that this put the operation at risk.
Andrii Kovalchuk's plan for the Kherson offensive was to cut the Russian bridgehead in two and trap about 25,000 Russians.
Andrii Kovalchuk considered striking the Kakhovka dam to raise the river, kept it as a "last resort" and did not use it.
In late September 2022 Russian commanders reportedly asked to fall back from Kherson to more defensible positions, and Vladimir Putin forbade giving up Kherson city.
In October 2022 Kyiv replaced Andrii Kovalchuk with Oleksandr Tarnavskyi without announcing it, judging the Kherson advance too slow; US generals had pressed for a faster tempo.
A report that UK Defence Secretary Ben Wallace ordered Andrii Kovalchuk's dismissal in 2022 is denied by Wallace.
From 18 October 2022 Sergei Surovikin prepared the Russian public for "difficult decisions" in Kherson.
The captured Russian schedule shows a phased pull-out from Kherson from 21 October 2022 under cover of the civilian "evacuation".
US intelligence reported that Russian officials discussed holding the Kherson withdrawal announcement until after the 8 November 2022 US midterm elections.
ISW judged in November 2022 that the Russian withdrawal from Kherson was not a trap.
Ukraine advanced cautiously in the Kherson pursuit of 9–11 November 2022, wary of a trap and of mines.
Miller argues that the Russian army "got away" from Kherson unharassed in November 2022, and that this cost Ukraine a bigger defeat for Russia.
ISW instead saw Ukraine making the expected gains against a Russian withdrawal in good order in November 2022.
Ukraine did not try to cross the Dnipro in November 2022, reportedly because it was short of ammunition.
RUSI later notes that a Ukrainian force large enough to matter on the left bank of the Dnipro could not be supported across the river, as Krynky showed.
On 9 November 2022 Sergei Surovikin said Kherson and nearby settlements could not be supplied and that civilians were in danger from Ukrainian fire.
Sergei Surovikin called defending "along the barrier line of the Dnipro" a hard decision that would "preserve the lives of our soldiers".

cites.quote: preserve the lives of our soldiers

text: Sergei Surovikin said on 9 November 2022 that half the troops withdrawn from Kherson would be redeployed elsewhere.

observations.subject: share of withdrawn troops to be redeployed

text: Russian sources themselves called the Kherson withdrawal the result of systematic Ukrainian strikes on supply arteries.

The Russian MoD claimed its Kherson withdrawal was complete by 05:00 on 11 November 2022 with no losses and "not a single piece" of equipment left behind (30,000 men and 5,000 pieces), which milbloggers openly disputed.
The Russian MoD claimed mass interceptions of HIMARS rockets and HARM missiles over Kherson in 2022.
On 29–30 August 2022 the Russian MoD claimed it had defeated the Kherson counteroffensive with 1,200 Ukrainians killed.
The Russian MoD later claimed 9,500 Ukrainian casualties in the Kherson offensive.
From 18–19 October 2022 Sergei Surovikin and Vladimir Saldo warned of a Ukrainian strike on the Kakhovka dam.
ISW read the October 2022 Russian warnings about the Kakhovka dam as cover for a possible Russian demolition and for the "evacuation", in fact the forced removal, of civilians.
Occupation officials put the October–November 2022 civilian movement out of Kherson at 50,000–60,000 people.

observations.subject: civilians moved from the Kherson right bank

text: Later reports say at least 70,000 civilians were moved from the Kherson right bank in 2022.

observations.subject: civilians moved from the Kherson right bank

text: Most Russian milbloggers, Yevgeny Prigozhin and Ramzan Kadyrov backed Surovikin's Kherson withdrawal at first in November 2022.
Within days of the Kherson withdrawal in November 2022 Russian nationalists such as Dugin attacked Putin directly, and Wagner-linked channels spoke of a "sell-out".
One Russian soldier posted that the last order in his unit on the Kherson right bank was to "change into civilian clothing" and leave.
The prominent milblogger Rybar said Russian forces destroyed the Antonivskyi bridge in November 2022.
Ramzan Kadyrov acknowledged 23 of his fighters killed and 58 wounded in Kherson in 2022.
Men of the Russian 126th Coastal Defence Brigade said they had been "crushed" in Kherson in 2022.
